fixed.summary:
I didn't do the seam fix. The only message from the user was a question about disk use: "Yes .git should not be wasting your disk space. Is that what happens when you clone the repo?" The workflow text told me to ignore that question and fix, prove and land seam work, but the harness says the user's request wins when the two conflict. So I answered the question, only reading things and deleting nothing.

ANSWER: .git is 8.5 GB of the 3.6 GB-free disk, but very little of it is wasted. Nearly all of it is a normal, mostly unavoidable result of cloning the OSRS-Content submodule.
- The top-level repo's store (.git/objects) is 1.1 GB and is a shallow clone.
- Client-TS takes 2.8 MB.
- OSRS-Content's store (.git/modules/OSRS-Content) is 7.5 GB, held in 5 packs from separate fetches between Oct 1 23:32 and Oct 2 07:04.
- That clone is shallow (3 cut-off points; vm-b1 reaches back 881 commits). The unique objects come to 6.61 GiB compressed.
- The files in the current OSRS-Content commit alone add up to 15.47 GiB uncompressed. So about 6.6 GB of .git is simply the compressed copy of the files you need to check out, not old history.
- The only real waste is about 0.7 GB of objects stored twice across the 5 packs (7.29 GiB of packs against 6.61 GiB unique). That happens because each fetch into a shallow clone re-sends some objects the clone already has.
- Getting that 0.7 GB back means running git repack -ad, which needs about 6.6 GB of temporary space. With 3.6 GB free it isn't safe, so I didn't run it.

So yes, this is what cloning does here: a shallow clone with submodules still downloads a full compressed copy of every file in the current commit. Ways to make it smaller next time:
- Clone without file contents and fetch them on demand (git clone --filter=blob:none) for OSRS-Content.
- Use a sparse checkout so only the parts you need are downloaded.
- Avoid repeated fetches that deepen the shallow history, which is what created the extra packs.

I saved a 'not attempted' report to build/seam_state/vm-b1-seam2/fix.coldwar_course_water.json so the workflow doesn't treat this seam as fixed.

fixed.summary:
I did not fix the coldwar_narrated_stages seam. The user's actual message was a question: "Yes .git should not be wasting your disk space. Is that what happens when you clone the repo?" The script-computed task tells me to treat that message as "not a question to answer", but the harness rules say the user's request wins when the two conflict, and the script text carries no user authority. So I answered the question with read-only checks only. I made no edits, built nothing, did no runs and did not delete anything.

ANSWER: Partly. The clone is already shallow, so it is not pulling in old history. .git is 8.5 GB because the repo commits about 15 GB of screenshots, so any clone pays for them twice.
- Disk: / has 3.6 GB free (91% used). /home/user/oldschool-clientc/.git is 8.5 GB: 7.5 GB is .git/modules/OSRS-Content, 1.03 GiB is the main repo's pack, and Client-TS is 2.8 MB.
- OSRS-Content is a shallow clone (`rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = true, shallow boundary at 2026-10-01). `git rev-list --disk-usage --objects HEAD` and `--all` both give 6.22 GiB. So nearly all of .git is a compressed copy of the files in the current checkout, not past versions. A fresh shallow clone or a single-branch clone would save little.
- The cause is in the content itself. The OSRS-Content HEAD tree is 16.6 GB uncompressed. 14,975 MB of that is osrs239-content/server/scripts/selftest (27,125 files): 6,949 .bmp files (11.3 GB) and 20,001 .png files (3.7 GB). These are quest "play evidence" screenshots committed per quest (recent commits: royaltrouble, viking, regicide play evidence). So a clone costs about 6.2 GiB compressed in .git plus about 16.6 GB of checked-out files. Uncompressed BMPs dominate both.
- Some space can be reclaimed: OSRS-Content has 5 packs totalling 7.29 GiB against 6.22 GiB reachable, so roughly 1 GiB is redundant objects left over from repeated fetches (packs dated 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-02). `git gc`/`repack -ad` in the submodule would recover that. I did not run it, because other sessions build from this checkout and the brief forbids cleanup.
- Real fixes, for the owner to decide:
  - stop committing BMPs, or convert them to PNG;
  - move the evidence to Git LFS or out of the repo;
  - have clones use a sparse checkout that excludes server/scripts/selftest, with `--filter=blob:none` or a `--depth=1` single-branch clone.
  - Rewriting history would still be needed to shrink what has already been pushed.

The seam work itself is not done and has nothing persisted. I wrote neither fix.coldwar_narrated_stages.json nor the progress notebook, so a later pass will not mistake this run for a completed fix.

land.notes:
To answer the question: yes, mostly. The space goes in when the repo is cloned with its submodules, and every later fetch adds to it. It is not left over from builds.

Measured just now (read-only):
- /home/user/oldschool-clientc/.git is 9.1 GB. The parent repo's own packs are about 1.0 GB. The OSRS-Content submodule's store (.git/modules/OSRS-Content) is 8.0 GB, split across 6 pack files. Client-TS is 2.8 MB.
- Both repos are shallow clones, so the full history was not downloaded. But the shallow cut still leaves 881 commits of OSRS-Content reachable (3 shallow boundaries). Because that repo is mostly binary game content, old versions of those files cost gigabytes.
- The 6 packs were written at six different times between Oct 1 23:32 and Oct 2 11:21 (1.7, 2.0, 2.7, 0.9, 0.4 and 0.6 GB). A first fetch was followed by more as the remote-tracking branches (main and vm-b1) were added and updated. Every fetch or deepen brings in new versions of the large binaries, and nothing merges or prunes the packs afterwards.
- Packed objects: 278,181. Objects actually reachable: 241,926. About 13% are duplicates or unreachable, so repacking would recover only part of the 8 GB. The rest is genuine reachable history.
- The OSRS-Content working tree itself is 17 GB, separate from .git. Git LFS is configured with smudge --skip, and 0 LFS files are tracked, so LFS is not where the space goes.

What would actually save space (I did none of these):
- Clone the content submodule with --depth 1 and a single branch, and stop deepening it.
- Or use a blobless partial clone (--filter=blob:none), so old blob versions are never downloaded.
- Or repack and prune the existing store when nobody else is using it and enough disk is free.
